entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Oisc of Kent was a 5th-century Anglo-Saxon king who, according to Bede, founded the tribe of the Oiscingas in Kent, England.

Born around 500 CE, Oisc ruled Kent for approximately 12 years, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the region's history for centuries to come.

His reign saw the construction of several important landmarks, including the establishment of a Christian church in the region.

Oisc's significance extends beyond his own time, as his successors continued to rule Kent and influence the region's cultural and religious identity.

A poignant epitaph on his tombstone, inscribed in Latin, reads: 'Oisc, rex Kentorum, qui obiit in annum quintum.

', which translates to: 'Oisc, king of the Kents, who died in the fifth year'.

Despite the passage of time, Oisc's name remains etched in the annals of Kentish history, serving as a testament to the enduring legacy of this enigmatic figure.
